fix_commit_message:
rtmp: fix double-free on URL parse errors

Reported-by: Stanislav Fort (Aisle Research)
Closes #19438
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 00872d5c98bf on top of intro cd3be116b688 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (DoubleFree): curl's RTMP protocol handler (lib/curl_rtmp.c) allocates an RTMP* handle and registers it into the connection's meta-data hash with a destructor (rtmp_conn_dtor) that will free it when the connection is torn down. If RTMP_SetupURL() subsequently fails to parse the target URL, rtmp_setup_connection() still performed a manual RTMP_Free(r) before returning an error, while the pointer remained registered in the connection meta store. When the connection was later destroyed, the registered destructor freed the same RTMP* a second time, producing a double-free that could be triggered remotely by any caller supplying a malformed rtmp:// URL. Root cause: When ownership/lifetime management of the RTMP* was moved to the connection meta-data hash (with an automatic destructor), the pre-existing manual free on the URL-parse-error early-return path was not removed, leaving two independent code paths (the manual free and the meta destructor) that both free the same object.
